identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Thiruvanaikaval is the Pancha Bhuta Sthalam of water, where Shiva is worshipped as Jambukeswarar together with the goddess Akilandeswari. HR&CE places the temple on the land between the Cauvery and the Kollidam and connects its name Jambukeswaram to an island covered with white jamun trees; the alternative name Thiruvanaikka refers to the white elephant said to have worshipped Shiva here.

narrative.summaryIntro:
Jambukeswarar Temple at Thiruvanaikaval, near Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, is one of the Pancha Bhoota Sthalams — the five Shiva temples representing the classical elements — where Shiva is worshipped as the element of water (Appu). The lingam in the sanctum stands over an underground spring, and the sanctum floor remains perpetually wet.

The temple, attributed to the early Chola king Kocengannan, is celebrated for its five prakaras, its shrine to the goddess Akilandeswari, and the unique noon ritual in which the priest, dressed as the goddess, performs worship to Jambukeswarar.
narrative.documentedHistory: The HR&CE department, which administers the temple, attributes its construction to the Chola king Kotchengan and records that the complex covers about eighteen acres on the land between the Cauvery and the Kollidam rivers. The department gives the name Jambukeswaram as deriving from an island covered with white jamun trees, and the alternative name Thiruvanaikka from the tradition of a white elephant that worshipped Shiva at the site. The deity is worshipped here under a long list of names recorded by the department, among them Appulingam, Sambunathar, Jambulingam, Amudheswarar, Sagaranyanathar and Aanaikka Annal, with the goddess as Akilanda Nayaki.
narrative.sthalaPuranam: HR&CE's account of the site connects the name Thiruvanaikka to a white elephant that worshipped Shiva there, and Jambukeswaram to an island of white jamun (naval) trees.

visitingInfo.nearestBusStation: City buses from Trichy and Srirangam (2 km)
visitingInfo.officialContactNote: HR&CE publishes this temple's darshan hours and pooja timings on its page at hrce.tn.gov.in (temple id 25706). The department's postal address for the temple is Thiruvanaikkaval, Thiruchirappalli 620005, and the office can be reached on 04312230257; confirm the day's schedule there, as festival days differ.

openingHours.notes: HR&CE states the temple is closed between 13:00 and 15:00 on Monday to Thursday.
HR&CE states the temple stays open through the middle of the day from Friday to Sunday, with no afternoon closure.
